name: Meat Science & Animal Products

objectives.text: Name common animal products such as meat, milk, eggs, wool, and leather and match each to the animal it comes from
Sort animal products into food products and nonfood by-products such as leather, gelatin, and wool
Describe the difference between a live animal and the meat products it provides after processing
Identify the industry names for meat from different species and ages, including beef, veal, pork, lamb, mutton, chevon, and poultry
Classify the primal and wholesale cuts of a beef, pork, or lamb carcass by their location on the animal
Explain how a muscle's location and use in the live animal affect the tenderness of the cut and the best cookery method
Explain the steps of the meat processing chain from harvest to fabrication to packaging, including the role of USDA inspection
Demonstrate safe handling of meat, milk, and eggs at home, including proper storage, safe internal cooking temperatures, and prevention of cross-contamination
Explain the conversion of muscle to meat, including rigor mortis and pH decline, and how preharvest stress and handling cause defects such as PSE pork and dark cutting beef
Summarize the characteristics of USDA quality grades and yield grades for beef, pork, and lamb carcasses
Calculate dressing percentage from live and hot carcass weights and explain the factors that cause it to vary
Analyze a meat or poultry package label for required components, including the inspection legend, safe handling instructions, and product name
Assign a beef quality grade from marbling and maturity scores and calculate a yield grade from fat thickness, ribeye area, hot carcass weight, and KPH
Analyze carcass yield grade and quality grade data, such as from a market animal SAE project, to evaluate carcass value and expected cutability
Identify retail meat cuts by species, primal cut, and recommended cookery method using muscle, bone, and fat characteristics as in the FFA Meats Evaluation CDE
Examine the quality factors of milk and eggs, including candling, egg grades, and milk quality tests, as used in grading and the FFA Milk Quality and Products CDE
Evaluate a wool fleece for grade, staple length, and yield and explain how these traits affect its market value
Evaluate and place classes of carcasses or retail cuts and defend the placings with oral reasons
Explain how curing, smoking, and emulsification use biochemical principles to produce processed meat products such as bacon, ham, and sausage
Analyze FSIS-approved antemortem and postmortem inspection procedures used during the harvest of livestock and poultry
Explain how the use of animal by-products contributes to sustainability and reduces waste in the meat industry
Evaluate food safety and quality-control procedures, including HACCP plans, used in a meat processing facility and justify improvements to reduce contamination risk
Create a value-added meat or animal product plan for an SAE or FFA project that addresses formulation, food safety, labeling, and cost

changes: Kept all six existing objectives with light rewording. Added early objectives on matching products to animals, food versus nonfood by-products, and species meat names. Added middle-grade objectives on muscle use and cookery, and safe home handling of meat, milk, and eggs. Added high school objectives on the conversion of muscle to meat, grade characteristics, dressing percentage, label analysis, assigning quality and yield grades, retail cut identification and carcass placing with oral reasons (Meats Evaluation CDE), milk and egg quality, wool evaluation, processed meat biochemistry, FSIS inspection, by-product sustainability, and a capstone value-added product SAE plan. Companion animals, aquaculture, and career or ethics content are left to sibling sub-topics.
